instructions: Continue only from the exact clean transportable RUN-241-001 failed candidate d05c33c14ffd7e5b6b468844df80ec833b14bc74. Do not restart PRIMARY from main and do not discard the already-passing 59 focused regression tests.

Runtime verification duration shows the live command terminated before the intended residual/full-suite experiment completed. This is not evidence that the historical 33 residual failures reproduced and it provides no valid TASK-241 classification.

Determine the exact live pre-execution/instrumentation mismatch using bounded transient local inspection. Candidate source shows early gates around exact subject lineage, historical identity reconstruction and installed-provenance baseline; these are hypotheses only. Do not assume any one is causal until reproduced in the real repair environment.

Correct only the diagnostic/observer contract so the unchanged TASK-241 experiment can faithfully enter Phase A under the actual self-host Python/pytest/xdist environment. Do not weaken fail-closed subject, privacy, identity, worker/process isolation, path-geometry, Git exact-once or observation-bound requirements merely to make the command exit zero.

In particular, reconcile any implementation assumption about installed-provenance baseline with the authored TASK-241 semantics: the observer is read-only, may report BASELINE_EXACT/CHANGED/MISSING/AMBIGUOUS/UNAVAILABLE relations as bounded facts, must never mutate installed Python state, and must distinguish a genuinely unusable/integrity-invalid baseline from a valid but non-ideal installed-state observation. If the concrete mismatch is elsewhere, fix that exact mismatch instead. Add focused regression coverage that reproduces the live mismatch discovered, preferably with a real subprocess/pytest boundary where the defect depends on actual interpreter/plugin behavior rather than only synthetic protocol dictionaries.

Preserve the TASK-241 execution surface exactly: collection/identity resolution first; one cold exact residual-33 n12 phase; only if Phase A passes, at most one full-suite n12 phase; workers=12, dist=load, max_worker_restart=0; selected-wrapper-equivalent 'aios-parallel-full-suite-' and 'parallel-12-tmp' geometry; no retry, fallback, n4/n8/n16 matrix or extra full-suite run.

Preserve typed/bounded Git and PUSH observation, same-worker predecessor/co-active context, read-only provenance relation observation, exact subject cleanliness/identity and all privacy/schema bounds. Do not modify any target test, fixture, production code, worker policy, Runtime/Reviewer/Publisher/workflows/carriers/roadmap or host configuration.
Runtime owns verification. The repaired candidate must be eligible for the exact original TASK-241 verification contract: focused diagnostic tests, the live diagnostic command, and git diff --check.

TASK-241 must retain bounded path-shape and typed Git failure facts without attributing cause in advance.

Runtime owns verification/evidence; Reviewer owns semantic verdict; Human owns worker selection and remediation risk acceptance. Diagnostic output cannot automatically unblock TASK-231 or choose a correction.

hard: Add one fixed no-argument command: 'python scripts/aios_residual_context_attribution_diagnostic.py'. Reject all positional/options input before test execution.
Require one clean exact canonical-main subject and prove its SHA remains unchanged before and after every phase. Any subject mutation or dirty state fails closed.

Perform one canonical collection-only phase first. Reconstruct the exact 33 historical residual selectors from the RUN-233-002-V002 safe identity/fingerprint algorithm and resolve them one-to-one against current collection. Missing, duplicate, ambiguous or changed identities must produce a bounded HISTORICAL_IDENTITY_DRIFT observation and stop before test execution; do not silently substitute current failures.

Phase A must execute exactly those 33 resolved residual selectors once at workers=12, distribution=load and max_worker_restart=0 in a fresh subprocess. Use the same TemporaryDirectory prefix 'aios-parallel-full-suite-' and the same 'parallel-12-tmp' basetemp label geometry as the TASK-231 selected full-suite wrapper so path-length evidence is not shortened by a diagnostic naming accident. No unrelated tests may execute in Phase A.
If Phase A reports any residual test failure, stop after Phase A and classify RESIDUAL_SET_N12_REPRODUCED. Do not run a full suite merely for additional ceremony.

Only if all 33 Phase A residual targets pass, Phase B may execute exactly one ordinary full-suite workers=12 run with distribution=load and max_worker_restart=0 in a separate fresh subprocess and independent 'aios-parallel-full-suite-' temporary root using the same 'parallel-12-tmp' basetemp geometry. No second full-suite execution is permitted.

Phase B must retain every unique failure identity up to a hard bound of 64. Zero failures classify FULL_SUITE_PASS_DRIFT. An exact failure set equal to the resolved historical 33 residual identities classifies FULL_SUITE_CONTEXT_REPRODUCED. Any nonempty different bounded failure set classifies FULL_SUITE_POPULATION_DRIFT. These classifications are observational only and must not choose a remediation.

For each residual target failure observed in either execution phase, retain only bounded safe facts: safe nodeid/fingerprint, pytest phase, worker label, exception type, stable message fingerprint, allowlisted repository-relative source locus, and bounded errno/winerror where applicable.

While an exact residual target protocol is active, transparently observe failing real Git subprocess operations by delegating each original invocation exactly once with unchanged argv/cwd/environment/check/text semantics. Persist only command family, integer return code, an allowlisted stderr category and bounded path-length facts derivable without exposing operands. Never retry, suppress, replace or repair a Git command.

For the exact Git fixture residual target, preserve TASK-240's specialized PUSH observation semantics: bounded ordinal/outcome/return-code, stderr-category on failure, ref length, remote-root length and derived remote-lock-path length, with no raw ref/path/URL/stderr/stdout.

Maintain a diagnostic-owned per-worker current-test registry containing only safe identities. For each residual failure in Phase B, persist a bounded snapshot of at most the other 11 co-active safe identities and at most four immediately preceding safe identities from the same worker. Registry instrumentation must not alter scheduling, insert barriers or delay tests.

Observe the real installed-provenance surface only as a read-only relation to a clean pre-execution baseline. Durable facts may state only BASELINE_EXACT, CHANGED, MISSING, AMBIGUOUS or UNAVAILABLE for the installed direct-url provenance, sitecustomize presence and aios-renew distribution multiplicity. Never persist their path or content. The diagnostic must make no writes to installed Python state.

The three source-audited global installed-provenance mutator nodeids may be exposed only as safe identities when they are present in a co-active snapshot. Their mere presence or overlap is evidence, not causality.

Validate exact collection/execution identity, all 12 worker identities, distinct process identities, isolated pytest basetemps, isolated process-local Git fixture cache roots and unchanged subject for every executed phase. Missing, malformed, contradictory, over-bound, privacy-unsafe or nonisolated observations fail closed.

The command exits zero when the bounded diagnostic completed faithfully, regardless of whether Phase A or Phase B observed pytest failures. Integrity, privacy, identity, subject or instrumentation failure exits nonzero.
No file outside the three scope.modify files may change.

task.problem: RUN-231-004 reached Runtime verification on the TASK-231 r2 adoption candidate 8908a7be6f190eeba0dff7d8fce03f9e892a4ecb with every selected-wrapper conformance fact true, but the n12 full suite reported 33 failures. Historical RUN-233-002 had reported 36 failures: 35 reproduced after that full-suite run in serial replay and all 36 at n4. TASK-234 then started from a fresh cold serial context and proved that only three of those 35 were serial-stable; the other 32 operator failures passed both target-only cold serial and complete two-file serial context. TASK-237 fixed two stable source-REPAIR failures and TASK-239 fixed the stable hot-swap Scenario 2 failure. Subtracting those three stable failures from the exact RUN-233-002 full-n12 set leaves exactly 33 historical residual identities: 32 tests/test_operator.py cases and one tests/test_git_fixture_isolation.py long-path PUSH case. RUN-231-004 reports the same failure count and its bounded first 20 identities match the ordered prefix of that historical residual set, but its transport surface truncates at 20 and therefore does not prove the complete current failure population. TASK-240 later observed the Git fixture target passing both serially and at n4 in isolation, so neither per-test production fixes nor a Git-path correction are currently justified. The missing evidence is whether the 33 residuals fail when they alone share an n12 process set, and, if they do not, what full-suite worker-local or shared external context is present when they fail.
